title: TE Brian Park et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Korean Central Presbytery’s April 14, 2021 action, and declared the underlying matter moot, ending it without remand.
first_summary: Teaching elders challenged Korean Central Presbytery’s summary censure of a minister before an indictment was prepared. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s action because discipline preceded particular charges and a specific confession, and because an independent church lacked authority to impose PCA censure. It declared the underlying matter moot because the alleged event was twenty-one years old and the victim would not cooperate, ending the proceeding without remand.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption and complaint decision appear at lines 11–15; the modified panel decision was approved by the SJC 17-1-1 at lines 137–139.
evidence_notes.dispute: Presbytery imposed summary discipline before preparation of an indictment; the stated issue challenged the manner of censure (lines 19–31, 39–45, 61–64).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The complaint was sustained, the lower-court action annulled, and the matter declared moot (lines 65–74). Presbytery lacked charges and a specific confession and improperly relied on non-PCA discipline (lines 99–133).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority expressly declined to address the allegations’ merits or hold that all twenty-one-year-old charges are unadjudicable (line 135). Separate opinions disputed mootness and remand (lines 144–170, 198–282).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No external decision was incorporated. The panel’s proposed remand was rejected by the SJC majority (lines 148–152).
